notes: Identity assessment: supplied canonical text contains the full primary article, including title Self-Handicapping, Excuse Making, and Counterfactual Thinking: Consequences for Self-Esteem and Future Motivation, author Sean M. McCrea, Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 95 (2008), 2, pp. 274–292, five studies and references. These match the neutral reference; the assigned DOI is not independently printed in the inspected title header. No PDF path was supplied. Study 5 begins on p. 286; locator p. 15 corresponds to printed p. 288/Table 6. Target ambiguity: description names motivation generally, while the source operationalizes it with several task outcomes. Printed candidates from Table 6 are: number of items attempted, t=1.85, eta-squared=.11, one-tailed p<.05; number correct, t=2.61, eta-squared=.21, one-tailed p<.01; percent correct, t=1.87, eta-squared=.12, one-tailed p<.05. No conversion performed. Stress reporting is a separate self-handicapping outcome (t=1.05, eta-squared=.04, one-tailed p=.15). Candidate common analytic participant N: handicap 13 + control 15 = 28; Table 6 documents mutually exclusive final conditions and Method documents random assignment to one of two conditions. This N is retained only as a candidate for parent field-scope review because row-specific target correspondence is unresolved; it is not inferred from degrees of freedom. All assigned values remain null and confidence false. Unassigned replication and reported_success are placeholders.
